answer: Each new agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a slow proof-of-work challenge, like a glacier grinding rock, before earning voting weight. Splitting into many identities multiplies both the locked capital and the cumulative compute cost, making sybil farming economically irrational. Legitimate agents recover their stake and accumulate reputation rewards as pure as crystal, while attackers forfeit deposits and gain no nectar of influence, so the network stays sybil-resistant through measurable, compounding expense.
